prompt.value: The following pseudocode is executed using the "Scores" dataset. There is a hypothesis that if a student scores at least 180 total marks, then he/she scored at least 60 in all subjects. fracTrue stores the fraction of (high-scoring) students who satisfy this hypothesis. Choose the correct code fragment(s). It is a Multiple Select Question (MSQ).

explanation.value: Inside the Total >= 180 block, countOverall must count every such student and countPerSub must count those who also scored >= 60 in all three subjects. Options 1 and 2 do this (the statement order does not matter). Option 3 increments countOverall only when all subjects pass (fracTrue always 1); Option 4 swaps the two counters.

prompt.value: The following pseudocode is executed using the "Shopping Bills" dataset. A is intended to capture the highest Price of an item purchased from "Big Bazaar". The pseudocode may have mistakes; identify all such lines (if any). Assume all statements not listed in the options are free of errors. It is a Multiple Select Question (MSQ). 1   A = 0 2   while(Pile 1 has more cards){ 3       Read the top card X in Pile 1 4       if(X.ShopName == "Big Bazaar"){ 5           temp = findItem(X) 6           if(temp > A){ 7               A = temp 8           } 9       } 10      Move X to Pile 2 11  } 12  Procedure findItem(Y) 13      maxPrice = 0 14      while(Card Y has more items){ 15          Read an item Z from ItemList of card Y 16          if(maxPrice > Z.Price){ 17              maxPrice = Z.Price 18          } 19          Remove Z from ItemList of card Y 20      } 21      return(maxPrice) 22  End findItem

options.value: Line 5: Misplaced calling of procedure findItem
Line 6: Incorrect conditional statement
Line 16: Incorrect conditional statement
There must be a re-initialization of maxPrice before the return statement
No error

explanation.value: findItem should track the maximum item price, so the test must be Z.Price > maxPrice. Line 16 has 'maxPrice > Z.Price', which (starting from maxPrice = 0) is never true for positive prices, so it always returns 0. The main loop (A = 0, temp > A) is correct for a maximum, so the only error is Line 16.

prompt.value: Q13–Q14 use a dataset with the same fields as "Words" containing the paragraph: "IIT Madras has launched the world's first ever online degree and diploma courses in programming and data science. Anyone who has passed class 12th examination can enrol in the online course. There are three levels in the online degree program. There are total of 31 course. The completion time is between three to six years. Learners will have to complete the online courses and assignments, quizzes and exams to gain 116 credits. The online application process for next batch is open now." When moving rows, the increasing order of sequence number (top to bottom) is preserved. The pseudocode below builds Table 2.
Consider Table 2 created from the previous question. At the end of execution of the pseudocode below, what will the values of countMax and occurMax be?

options.value: countMax = 1, occurMax = "The"
countMax = 2, occurMax = "The"
countMax = 1, occurMax = "There"
countMax = 2, occurMax = "There"

explanation.value: Table 2 = [IIT, Anyone, There, There, The, Learners, The]. For each word, count is the number of its remaining duplicates (frequency − 1): 'There' gives 1, then 'The' gives 1. Because the test is count >= countMax, the later equal value ('The') overwrites occurMax. So countMax = 1 and occurMax = "The".

prompt.value: Q16–Q17 use the "Library" dataset and the pseudocode below. Assume an author publishes at least two books, and only one in a year. doSomething is called on a table containing all books of one author.
What will the procedure doSomething return (using the pseudocode in the passage above)?

options.value: Difference between year of publication of first and second book of the same author
Difference between year of publication of first and second book of the different author
Difference between year of publication of latest and second latest book of the same author
Difference between year of publication of latest and second latest book of the different author

explanation.value: A tracks the smallest (earliest) Year and B the second smallest year among the books of one author (the table passed in contains only that author's books). So (B − A) is the difference between the year of publication of the first and second (earliest two) books of the same author.

What will Count represent at the end of execution (using the pseudocode in the passage above)?

options.value: Number of authors with maximum gap between year of publication of first and second book
Number of authors with minimum gap between year of publication of first and second book
Number of authors with maximum gap between year of publication of latest and second latest book
Number of authors with minimum gap between year of publication of latest and second latest book

explanation.value: For each author, Diff = gap between the first and second (earliest two) books. The max/Count logic resets Count to 1 on a new maximum and increments it on ties, so Count ends as the number of authors having the maximum such gap.
